title: Locally constant sheaf reduction
statement:
Let $r$ be a prime number and let $U$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-irreducible-components] (so $U$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]). Let $G$ be a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-vector spaces on the small etale site $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]: a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] which is etale locally isomorphic, as a sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules, to the constant sheaf $\underline M$ of a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_r$-vector space $M$ (a finite type, locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules in the sense of Stacks 03RU and 0A3R). Then there are a connected scheme $V$, a finite etale morphism $v:V\to U$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and an integer $d\ge1$ not divisible by $r$ such that:

1. *(degree)* $v$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and every geometric fibre of $v$ has exactly $d$ points;
2. *(filtration)* the inverse image $v^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] has a finite filtration $0=G_0\subseteq G_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_m=v^{-1}G$ by subsheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules with $G_i/G_{i-1}\cong\underline{\mathbf F_r}_V$ (the constant sheaf with value $\mathbf F_r=\mathbf Z/r$) for $1\le i\le m$;
3. *(trace splitting)* with $\eta=\operatorname{res}_{v,G}:G\to v_*v^{-1}G$ the unit of the adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $\operatorname{tr}=\operatorname{tr}_{v,G}:v_*v^{-1}G\to G$ the trace of the finite etale $v$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace],

$$
 G\xrightarrow{\eta}v_*v^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}}G
 \;=\;d\cdot\operatorname{id}_G ,
$$

so that, $d$ being invertible on the $\mathbf F_r$-sheaf $G$, $p=d^{-1}\operatorname{tr}$ satisfies $p\circ\eta=\operatorname{id}_G$ and $G$ is a direct summand of $v_*v^{-1}G$: $v_*v^{-1}G=\eta(G)\oplus\ker p$ as sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules.

proof.text: *The representation (Stacks 0A3R, proof, first paragraph).* An irreducible space is nonempty and connected (a decomposition into two disjoint nonempty open subsets would contradict that any two nonempty opens meet). Choose a point $u\in U$ and the geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(u)}\to U$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $\pi_1=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ be the profinite group of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations] (1) with $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$ ($U$ connected), $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar u}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is an exact equivalence between finite locally constant sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ and finite $\mathbf F_r$-modules with a continuous $\mathbf F_r$-linear $\pi_1$-action, carrying $\underline{\mathbf F_r}_U$ to the trivial representation $\mathbf F_r$. Put $M=G_{\bar u}$, a finite $\mathbf F_r$-vector space, and let $\rho:\pi_1\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_r}(M)$ be the action. Its image $Q=\rho(\pi_1)$ is a finite group, because $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_r}(M)$ is a group of permutations of the finite set $M$. Its kernel $\ker\rho=\bigcap_{m\in M}\operatorname{Stab}_{\pi_1}(m)$ is a finite intersection of open subgroups (the action on the discrete $M$ is continuous), hence an open normal subgroup of $\pi_1$.

*The Sylow subgroup (Stacks 0A3R, proof).* By [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index] the finite group $Q$ has an $r$-subgroup $P$ (a finite $r$-group) with $r\nmid[Q:P]$. Put $H=\rho^{-1}(P)\subseteq\pi_1$. It is a subgroup containing the open subgroup $\ker\rho$, hence a union of cosets of $\ker\rho$, hence open. Since $\rho:\pi_1\to Q$ is surjective, $gH\mapsto\rho(g)P$ is a bijection $\pi_1/H\to Q/P$, so $d:=[\pi_1:H]=[Q:P]$ is finite, $d\ge1$ and $r\nmid d$.

source.place: Stacks Lemma 0A3R, proof: 'Let $H\subset G$ be an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup ... the degree of $T=Y/H\to S$ is prime to $\ell$ as it is equal to the index of $H$ in $G$'

proof.text: *The connected cover $v$ (Stacks 0A3R: $T=Y/H$; Fundamental Groups, Section 03SF).* The finite set $S=\pi_1/H$ with the action by left translation is a finite $\pi_1$-set with continuous action (the stabilizer of $gH$ is the open subgroup $gHg^{-1}$), and the action is transitive. (In Stacks, $S=G/H$ is the fibre of $T=Y/H$, $Y$ the Galois object of $\pi_1\to Q$; we take the object with fibre $S$ directly.) By [thm-galois-fundamental] ($U$ connected) the fibre functor $F_{\bar u}:P\mapsto|P_{\bar u}|$ [def-galois-categories] is an equivalence $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(U)\to\pi_1\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ compatible with finite limits and colimits, so there is a finite etale $v:V\to U$ with an equivariant bijection $F_{\bar u}(V)\cong S$. $V$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]: it is nonempty, since $S\ne\varnothing$ while $F_{\bar u}(\varnothing)=\varnothing$; and if $V=V_1\sqcup V_2$ with $V_1,V_2$ open and closed, then $V_j\to V\to U$ is finite etale (an open and closed immersion is finite etale), $V$ is the coproduct of $V_1,V_2$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(U)$, so $S=F_{\bar u}(V_1)\sqcup F_{\bar u}(V_2)$ as $\pi_1$-sets; by transitivity one of them, say $F_{\bar u}(V_2)$, is empty, so $F_{\bar u}(V_2)\cong F_{\bar u}(\varnothing)$ and, the equivalence reflecting isomorphisms, $V_2\cong\varnothing$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree] ($U$ connected) $v$ is finite locally free of some degree $d'$ and every geometric fibre of $v$ has $d'$ points; at $\bar u$ the fibre has $\#F_{\bar u}(V)=\#S=d$ points, so $d'=d$. This is assertion 1.

source.place: Stacks Lemma 0A3R, proof ('We claim that $T=Y/H\to S$ works'); Fundamental Groups Section 03SF (pione-section-finite-etale-under-galois) and Theorem 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group)

proof.text: *The monodromy of $v^{-1}G$ is $P$ (Stacks 0A3R: 'the image of $\pi_1(T,\bar t)\to\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ is $\overline\rho^{-1}(H)$'; Remark 0DV6).* Let $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(u)}\to V$ be the geometric point over $\bar u$ that corresponds to the coset $H\in S\cong F_{\bar u}(V)$ (points of the geometric fibre $V_{\bar u}$ are lifts of $\bar u$). By [thm-galois-fundamental], compatibility with base change along the connected $V\to U$: pullback $P\mapsto P\times_UV$ of finite etale covers, with $F_{\bar v}(P\times_UV)=F_{\bar u}(P)$, induces a continuous homomorphism $\varphi:\pi_1(V,\bar v)\to\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ whose image is the stabilizer of the point $\bar v$ of $F_{\bar u}(V)$, i.e. the open subgroup $H$; and by [thm-galois-lc-etale] (compatibility with base change and with the fibre functors) the $\pi_1(V,\bar v)$-set $(v^{-1}\mathcal A)_{\bar v}$ of a finite locally constant sheaf of sets $\mathcal A$ on $U$ is $\mathcal A_{\bar u}$ with $\sigma$ acting as $\varphi(\sigma)$. The identification of stalks $c:(v^{-1}G)_{\bar v}\cong G_{\bar u}=M$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]; it is additive and $\mathbf F_r$-linear, the module operations of $v^{-1}G$ being the inverse images of those of $G$ ($v^{-1}$ commutes with finite products). Hence the representation of $\pi_1(V,\bar v)$ attached to $v^{-1}G$ by [cor-galois-lisse-representations] (1) on the connected $V$ is $M$ with $\sigma$ acting by $\rho(\varphi(\sigma))\in\rho(H)=P$.

source.place: Stacks Lemma 0A3R, proof ('the action of $\pi_1(T,\bar t)$ on $V$ corresponding to $f^{-1}\mathcal F$ is through the map $\pi_1(T,\bar t)\to H$'); Remark 0DV6 (remark-functorial-locally-constant-on-connected)

proof.text: *The filtration (Stacks 0A3R, proof; Lemma 0GIZ).* $M$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_r[P]$-module ($P\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_r}(M)$ acting by inclusion). By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-l-group-filtration] ($P$ a finite $r$-group) there is a $P$-stable filtration $0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_m=M$ with each $M_i/M_{i-1}$ the trivial one-dimensional representation $\mathbf F_r$ (if $M=0$, $m=0$). As $\pi_1(V,\bar v)$ acts on $M$ through $P$ (step 4), each $M_i$ is a sub-representation and $M_i/M_{i-1}\cong\mathbf F_r$ with trivial $\pi_1(V,\bar v)$-action. Apply the exact equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] (1) on $V$ (connected, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$), whose kernels and cokernels are those of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules: by essential surjectivity and full faithfulness there are finite locally constant $\mathbf F_r$-sheaves $G'_i$ with $(G'_i)_{\bar v}\cong M_i$, maps $G'_{i-1}\to G'_i$ inducing the inclusions $M_{i-1}\subset M_i$, and $G'_m\cong v^{-1}G$ (step 4). The kernel of $G'_{i-1}\to G'_i$ goes to $\ker(M_{i-1}\to M_i)=0$, so it is $0$ and the map is a monomorphism; let $G_i\subseteq v^{-1}G$ be the image of $G'_i$ under the composite monomorphism $G'_i\to G'_m\cong v^{-1}G$. The cokernel $G_i/G_{i-1}$ goes to $M_i/M_{i-1}\cong\mathbf F_r$ with trivial action, which is the image of $\underline{\mathbf F_r}_V$; by full faithfulness $G_i/G_{i-1}\cong\underline{\mathbf F_r}_V$. Also $G_0=0$ and $G_m=v^{-1}G$. This is assertion 2.

source.place: Stacks Lemma 0A3R, proof ('As $H$ is a finite $\ell$-group, the irreducible constituents ... are each trivial of rank 1 ... Via the equivalence of Lemma 0DV5 this means $f^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a successive extension of constant sheaves'); Lemma 0GIZ (lemma-action-l-group)

proof.text: *The trace (Stacks Section 03SH).* Let $\eta=\operatorname{res}_{v,G}$ be the unit of $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $\operatorname{tr}=\operatorname{tr}_{v,G}$ the trace of the finite etale $v$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace], both applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree] ($U$ connected, $v$ of constant degree $d$ by step 3), $\operatorname{tr}\circ\eta=d\cdot\operatorname{id}_G$. Both maps are additive maps between sheaves of $\mathbf Z/r=\mathbf F_r$-modules, hence $\mathbf F_r$-linear.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), after Definition 03SE ('if $f$ has constant degree $d$, then the composition $\mathcal F\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is multiplication by $d$')

proof.text: *Direct summand (Stacks Section 03SH: 'if multiplication by $d$ on $\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism').* $rG=0$ and $r\nmid d$, so there is $e\in\mathbf Z$ with $de\equiv1\pmod r$ and multiplication by $d$ on $G$ (and on $v_*v^{-1}G$) is invertible with inverse multiplication by $e$. Then $p=e\cdot\operatorname{tr}$ satisfies $p\circ\eta=ed\cdot\operatorname{id}_G=\operatorname{id}_G$ by step 6, so $\eta$ is a split monomorphism in the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $\eta\circ p$ is an idempotent endomorphism of $v_*v^{-1}G$ with image $\eta(G)\cong G$ and kernel $\ker p$, and $v_*v^{-1}G=\eta(G)\oplus\ker p$. This is assertion 3.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For irreducible $U$ and finite locally constant $G$ of
$\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces, there is a finite etale
$v:V\to U$ of degree prime to $\ell$ such that $v^{-1}G$ has a filtration by
constant $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaves, and $G$ is a direct summand of
$v_*v^{-1}G$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$. The locally constant sheaf gives
a representation

$$
\rho:\pi_1(U,\bar u)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf F_\ell}(G_{\bar u})
$$

with finite image $Q$. If $H\subseteq Q$ is an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup, the
inverse image $\rho^{-1}(H)$ defines a connected finite etale cover
$v:V\to U$ of degree $d=[Q:H]$, which is prime to $\ell$. On $V$, the
monodromy factors through $H$.

The representation filtration gives
$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_m=G_{\bar u}$ with
$V_a/V_{a-1}\cong\mathbf F_\ell$ and trivial $H$-action. Passing from
$H$-modules to locally constant sheaves gives, for every $a$, the explicit
short exact sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow G_{a-1}\longrightarrow G_a\longrightarrow
\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}_V\longrightarrow0,
\qquad G_m=v^{-1}G.
$$

All inclusions, quotient maps, and connecting maps commute with extension of
the algebraically closed ground field.

The adjunction unit and the fibrewise sum are

$$
\eta:G\longrightarrow v_*v^{-1}G,\qquad
\operatorname{tr}:v_*v^{-1}G\longrightarrow G.
$$

At a geometric stalk, $\eta(s)=(s,\ldots,s)$ in the direct sum indexed by
the $d$ points of the fibre, while
$\operatorname{tr}(s_1,\ldots,s_d)=\sum_as_a$. Consequently
$\operatorname{tr}\circ\eta=d\,\operatorname{id}_G$. Multiplication by
$d^{-1}\in\mathbf F_\ell$ defines
$r=d^{-1}\operatorname{tr}$ with $r\eta=\operatorname{id}_G$.
The stalk formulas are preserved by base change, so the direct-summand
decomposition and every filtration exact sequence are compatible with the
cohomology comparison maps.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise without changing the mathematics: prime r named, U a scheme (irreducible, hence nonempty and connected), G a finite locally constant sheaf of F_r-vector spaces (etale locally the constant sheaf of a finite F_r-module; Stacks 03RU/0A3R), V connected and v finite etale of degree d (finite locally free of degree d, every geometric fibre has d points) with r not dividing d, the filtration written out (0=G_0 c ... c G_m=v^{-1}G, G_i/G_{i-1} = constant F_r), eta the adjunction unit and tr the trace of a new definition node, and the direct-summand conclusion with the retraction d^{-1} tr.
